profiles.meeting_scenario: A planning meeting at a quantitative asset management firm between the lead quantitative researcher and the product strategy manager to map a six-week internal rollout for a new research note and pilot allocator based on an asymptotically optimal portfolio strategy in a slowly varying stochastic environment. The trigger is that the research team now has a rigorous first-order approximation result and an asymptotic optimality claim beyond prior heuristic work, and leadership wants a package ready for the next internal investment committee cycle so they can decide whether to sponsor engineering work for the model portfolio platform. The agenda is to align on what the month-end 'working prototype for the platform' should consist of, what comparison baseline will appear in the committee materials, what work is meant by 'finalizing the committee deck,' how the solvable model should be included, and who owns each deliverable and milestone. The expected outcome is a concrete plan with deliverables, owners, dependencies, and dates for the technical note, baseline comparison package, prototype outputs, and committee materials.

members.name: Daniel Wu
members.expertise: stochastic control, portfolio optimization, asymptotic methods, model validation
members.background: Daniel has a PhD in applied mathematics and leads the firm's systematic macro research pod; he regularly translates academic portfolio theory into internal research frameworks and is known for insisting that any rollout preserve the exact conditions under which a result is valid.
members.private_state: He wants to protect the mathematical integrity of the result, avoid committing his team to quasi-production work before the theory is properly documented, and keep the rollout narrow enough that it does not derail an unrelated live strategy review already on his calendar.
hidden_assumptions: A 'working prototype for the platform' means research output formatted so platform engineers could ingest it later—weight files, parameter tables, and documented logic—but not something already visible inside the portfolio platform UI.
When people say 'the baseline' for this strategy, they mean the internal Merton-style research benchmark notebook that serves as the natural zeroth-order comparison for asymptotic improvements.

Most of the remaining work in 'finalizing the committee deck' is actually finishing the technical appendix: proofs, assumptions, and approximation-error exhibits that make the headline claims defensible.

To 'include the solvable model' means adding a concise tractable example that verifies the paper's assumptions in a fully solvable specification, mainly as mathematical support rather than a stand-alone business artifact.

members.name: Priya Raman
members.expertise: portfolio productization, internal stakeholder alignment, launch planning, investment committee preparation
members.background: Priya previously worked in institutional solutions and now sits between quant research, engineering, and portfolio managers; she is experienced in turning technically dense strategies into internal pilot proposals that can secure governance approval and implementation resources.
members.private_state: She wants a credible committee package that can unlock engineering bandwidth next quarter, and she is trying to frame the work as an operationally plausible platform enhancement rather than a purely academic extension with uncertain adoption.
hidden_assumptions: A 'working prototype for the platform' means something stakeholders can already view in the model portfolio platform environment, even if it is a thin mock-up or manually refreshed demonstration rather than a fully automated build.

When people say 'the baseline,' they mean the current diversified growth sleeve that PMs already recognize from allocation discussions, because that is the only comparison that will matter in committee.
The main work in 'finalizing the committee deck' is polishing the executive summary, implementation path, and decision-ready charts, with technical detail staying in backup slides unless challenged.

To 'include the solvable model' means providing a concrete calibrated example with realistic-looking inputs and output charts that can stand on its own in the deck and help non-quants picture how the idea behaves.

misalignment_points.topic: What a 'working prototype for the platform' actually is
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both agree to have a 'working prototype for the platform' by month-end.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means research-grade deliverables packaged for eventual platform ingestion: reproducible weight-generation code, sample output files, and documentation of the slowly varying factor logic for engineering handoff.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means a stakeholder-visible artifact already sitting in the platform environment or a close facsimile of it, so PMs can click through a model portfolio view before the committee meeting.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase feels specific enough to remove ambiguity because both hear the same anchor words—'working,' 'prototype,' and 'for the platform'—yet each silently resolves 'for the platform' through their own function: one as upstream compatibility, the other as downstream visibility.

misalignment_points.topic: Which comparison is meant by 'the baseline'
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both say the strategy should be shown 'against the baseline' in the committee materials.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is referring to the firm's internal Merton-style research benchmark notebook used to compare the zeroth-order strategy with the asymptotic improvement in a mathematically coherent way.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is referring to the live diversified growth sleeve currently used by portfolio managers as the practical point of comparison for any proposed platform enhancement.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Within each person's workflow, there really is one obvious baseline, so the definite article sounds natural and complete; because both expect the other to know the standard reference, the mismatch hides behind everyday shorthand.

misalignment_points.topic: What work remains in 'finalizing the committee deck'
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that the next major milestone is 'finalizing the committee deck' before the review date.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes this milestone is met once the technical appendix, proof-backed assumptions, and approximation-error exhibits are complete enough that the deck's claims are defensible if scrutinized.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes this milestone is met once the executive storyline, implementation timeline, and decision-oriented charts are polished enough for committee circulation, even if some technical backup keeps evolving.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Because both are talking about the same named artifact—the committee deck—the conversation appears concrete; the hidden divergence is not about whether a deck exists, but about which part of the deck constitutes the real remaining work.

misalignment_points.topic: What is included in 'including the solvable model'
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both agree to 'include the solvable model' in the rollout package.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes this means a compact technical section showing that the asymptotic framework's assumptions hold in a particular fully solvable specification, mainly to support the theorem-level narrative.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes this means a presentable example with calibrated parameters, sample allocations, and performance visuals that can function as a concrete demonstration for stakeholders.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds like a minor content inclusion rather than a scope choice, so neither person treats it as something requiring unpacking; each assumes the other's version is simply the obvious way one 'includes' an example.

If we can get a stakeholder-visible prototype into the model portfolio environment by month-end, PMs can react to something concrete before the committee cycle.
